subject: Food Science
title: Shelf Life Testing
description: A 60-second lesson on Shelf Life Testing.

hook.text: 'Best before' dates aren't safety dates—they're quality estimates. Manufacturers use accelerated testing to predict how long food.

buildup.text: Real-time testing stores products under normal conditions and evaluates them periodically.

discovery.text: Accelerated shelf life testing (ASLT) stores food at elevated temperature. Reactions speed up ~2x per 10°C increase, predicting.

twist.text: 'Use by' dates are safety dates—ignore them at your risk. 'Best before' dates are quality dates.

climax.text: 30% of food waste is driven by consumers discarding food past 'best before' dates that are safe and nutritious.

punchline.text: 'Use by' means safety. 'Best before' means quality. Confusing them wastes 30% of food.

quiz.question: How does accelerated shelf life testing work?
options: Elevated temperature speeds reactions ~2x per 10°C—predicting years of aging in weeks
